identification.summary: "Unnamed Actor" is a placeholder entry in the CFR Cyber Operations Tracker, mirrored in MISP Galaxy and Malpedia, describing a suspected China-linked actor that compromises civil society groups the Chinese Communist Party regards as hostile (Tibetan, Uyghur, Hong Kong and Taiwanese activists) and that also targeted the Myanmar electoral commission [S3]. The entry is not a vendor-defined cluster and no malware families are listed for it [S3].
identification.firstObserved: Not established. The earliest related public reporting found is Citizen Lab Report #65 (2015-10) [S1]; no dated incident in the tracker entry could be tied to open sources.
identification.notes: The tracker entry is a composite label. Citizen Lab reports on a Burma-focused NGO campaign [S1] and the UP007/SLServer campaign against Hong Kong activists [S2] describe related TTP overlap, not a confirmed match to this entry. Do not merge with Scarlet Mimic, EvilEye/Earth Empusa, PKPLUG, Mustang Panda or Red Echo without vendor support.

attribution.sponsor: China (suspected, per CFR Cyber Operations Tracker data as mirrored in MISP Galaxy) [S3]
attribution.confidence: Low. The suspected-state-sponsor field comes from a secondary tracker; no government attribution was found and no vendor attribution could be tied to this exact entry [S3].
attribution.basis: The entry classifies the incident type as espionage, with suspected victims China, Myanmar, Hong Kong and Taiwan, and categories civil society and government [S3]. Primary CFR page could not be opened [S3].

objectives: Espionage against civil society and government targets perceived as hostile to the CCP, per the tracker's incident type and target categories [S3].

sectors: Civil society (Tibetan, Uyghur, Hong Kong and Taiwanese activists) [S3]
targeting.notes: Citizen Lab Report #65 tied a targeted malware campaign against a Southeast Asian environmental NGO to compromises of Burmese government websites and earlier campaigns against Tibetan groups [S1]. Citizen Lab later linked UP007 malware, first noted by Arbor ASERT in samples hosted on the Myanmar Union Election Commission site, to a campaign against Hong Kong democracy activists [S2]. These are related reports, not confirmed to be this entry.

capabilities.summary: The tracker entry lists no malware families [S3]. Related Citizen Lab reporting describes the UP007 and SLServer malware families against Hong Kong activists [S2]; the link of these tools to this entry is unconfirmed.

campaigns.name: Targeted malware campaign against Southeast Asian environmental NGO
campaigns.summary: Citizen Lab Report #65 (published 2015-10-16) described email lures themed on Burmese economic development and politics, linked to strategic web compromises of Burmese government websites and earlier campaigns against Tibetan groups [S1]. Relationship to the tracker entry is unconfirmed.

campaigns.name: UP007 and SLServer campaign against Hong Kong activists
campaigns.summary: Citizen Lab Report #74 examined espionage against Hong Kong democracy activists using UP007 and SLServer; UP007 was first noted by Arbor ASERT in samples hosted on the Myanmar UEC site, and the report notes TTP overlap with operations against groups in Burma, Hong Kong and the Tibetan community [S2]. Relationship to the tracker entry is unconfirmed.

diamond.adversary: Suspected China-linked espionage actor; no named group or organization [S3].
diamond.capability: No tracker-listed malware [S3]; related reporting shows UP007/SLServer [S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Compromised legitimate website (Myanmar UEC) hosted UP007 samples [S2]; Burmese government websites were compromised in related activity [S1].
diamond.victim: Tibetan, Uyghur, Hong Kong and Taiwanese civil society and the Myanmar electoral commission [S3].
diamond.socioPolitical: Targets are groups the CCP views as hostile to its interests [S3].
diamond.technology: Strategic web compromise and malware delivery; email phishing with Burma-themed lures in related reporting [S1][S2].

gaps: Primary CFR Cyber Operations Tracker page and the Malpedia entry could not be opened (host blocked); details rely on search-result summaries of MISP Galaxy mirrors [S3].
No dates, malware, or vendor name for the Tibetan, Uyghur, Taiwanese activist targeting in this entry were found.
Whether this entry corresponds to the actor behind the Burma-related NGO and UP007 activity is unverified; Citizen Lab did not name a group [S1][S2].
Possible overlaps with EvilEye, Scarlet Mimic, PKPLUG and Red Echo (Myanmar presidential website, 2021) are unassessed [S4].

Citizen Lab pages could not be fetched; facts come from search summaries. S3 commit month not confirmed (reported only as 2018). A prior claim of PlugX on the UEC site in 2015-08 could not be confirmed and was removed.
